newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Top Russian official meets royal relative.
newsitem.headline: Top Russian official meets royal relative.

text.p: Russia's first deputy prime minister met the grandmother of one of the claimants to the Russian imperial throne on Saturday, NTV commercial television reported.
Boris Nemtsov told the station he met Grand Duchess Leonida Georgyevna as part of the government's discussions on what to do with the remains of Tsar, Nicholas II and his family.

Revolutionary Bolsheviks killed Nicholas II and his family in 1918, a year after he abdicated his throne. Their remains are now locked in the morgue in Yekaterinburg, the Ural Mountains city where they were shot.

"The burial is an intimate matter for the relatives and for the Russian Orthodox Church to decide, as there is talk of canonisation," Nemtsov said, when asked his opinion about what the government should do.

The grand duchess, now in her 80s, lives in Madrid but wants to gain an official status for her family in Russia. Her grandson, Grand Duke Georgy Romanov, 16, is one of several relatives who claim the right to inherit the throne.
